context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Stop serialising the whole `updatedUser` model. Build the response from an explicit allow-list of fields the client needs, for example `res.json({ user: toUserResponse(updatedUser) })`, where `toUserResponse` returns only fields such as `id`, `name`, and `avatarUrl`. Exclude sensitive or internal fields such as `passwordHash`, tokens, MFA secrets, internal flags, and nested records the requester is not entitled to see. Define the serializer once, in a shared module, and use it on every route that returns this user record so the field limits stay consistent. Add a test that asserts the response contains only the allow-listed keys and none of the excluded ones.
